{{short description|Panamanian sociologist, statistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=January 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=January 2021}}
'''Ana G. Casís''' was a Panamanian sociologist, statistician, and demographer who directed the 1950 Panamanian census, and later worked for the Inter-American Statistical Institute in Washington, DC.{{r|archer}} She is also known for her work with [[Kingsley Davis]] on [[urbanization]] in [[Latin America]],{{r|ula}} Davis's first work on urbanization.{{r|davis}}

Casís earned a bachelor's degree in Panama in 1943, and a master's degree at [[Syracuse University]] in 1945, with the master's thesis "Population studies in Mexico, Panama, and Puerto Rico, with special reference to urbanization processes.{{r|socdiss}}

In 1979, she was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}}

She died before 2012, when she was listed as a deceased former member by the Washington Statistical Society.{{r|wss}}
